newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP approves directive on distance selling.
newsitem.headline: EP approves directive on distance selling.

text.p: Europe's direct marketing and financial services industries now have clear operating rules following the European Parliament's approval on Thursday of a new directive on distance selling.

MEPs only agreed to the directive -- COM(92)11 -- which is designed to protect consumers offered goods or services by phone, fax, TV or mail order, after three months of negotiations with the Council of Ministers.
The talks resulted in nearly all of parliament's amendments to the text being taken on board.

By way of a compromise, parliament dropped an earlier demand for telemarketers to seek prior consent from consumers before unsoliticted attempts to sell them goods and services over the phone or by e-mail, because of the difficulty of making this work in practice.
Instead, they accepted a solution which obliges tele-salespeople to identify themselves and seek permission before launching into their sales bid.
They must also give potential consumers clear advance details of the proposed contract, and confirm this information in writing after the sale has taken place.

To the relief of the financial services industry, parliament accepted the new rules should not cover financial services, in return for a pledge from the European Commission to draft separate legislation in this field.
But credit card payments over the phone will fall within the directive's scope.
Consumers will now have seven working days to change their minds about purchases not made face-to-face, especially mail order goods paid for by cheque or credit card.
Suppliers will have to refund dissatisfied customers within 30 days.
The measures wil only apply to sales calls coming from another European Union member state.
